question: One law, two ways of satisfying it. What does each cost?
graph: the frozen EUR-Lex truth with 3,932 injected wrong type labels, runs/seven/journal.json
the law: L6 — an act's type label says what its CELEX says: 32019R1020 is a Regulation

deletion-only repair (pgrepair, SciPyWei.note: two buckets of one judge over the same event, not two costs to add

one Cypher statement per type pair.does: sets the label the CELEX dictates and removes the one that contradicts it

and the honest reading, which is not tha: The Cypher repair uses a piece of DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE — that the CELEX is the authority on the type. pgrepair works from the constraints alone and is a general engine. It is not the same game, and this is not a criticism of it.

What it shows is WHERE THE TRUTH LIVES. The type was written twice in the document, once as a label and once inside the identifier, and the construction pipeline carried both into the graph. That second witness is the whole reason a repair can put the label right instead of deleting the node. A constraint engine cannot know which of two contradicting values is the authority.

So the rule generalises: a downstream repair can mend a fault exactly when a SECOND, independent witness of the fact survived into the graph. Where the assembly carried one witness only, nothing downstream can, whatever it is written in.
and its limit, measured on the same grap: 68,525 of 264,937 nodes carry no celex_type at all — a quarter of the graph. A wrong label there is beyond the Cypher repair too, and beyond anything else in the graph. The second witness is not a property of the method; it is a property of what was carried.
a prediction registered before the run,: Predicted that Cypher would put 3,932 labels right. It puts 3,930: two of the injected labels are invisible to the CELEX check, and they are the same two pgrepair does not reach either.
